images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of CHORD. CHORD separates proposing biases from testing them for reliable bias discovery in the target model. First, each view proposes a candidate bias. The intuition is that a noisy candidate bias pattern in one representation may be denoised in another. Each candidate partitions samples into majority and outlier subsets. We then test the candidate in the target space by removing the feature difference between the two subsets. Removing a real bias improves within-class compactness by moving outliers closer to their class centroid. Outliers whose nearest-centroid assignments return to their labeled class are used as minority candidates. Finally, we aggregate this evidence across views to retrain the classifier head.
